**Important distinction first:** the document you pasted is a **findings + prioritization + decision ledger**, not an **implementation plan** in the writing-plans sense. That mismatch is the main feedback. Below is author review against the writing-plans bar and against what an engineer with zero context would need.

---

# Feedback: Repo state consistency + alignment plan

## What this document is good at

**1. Verdict is load-bearing and memorable.**  
The one-paragraph diagnosis (“self-referential spiral with one real product win”) and the stop-list in P3 give an owner a clear posture. That is rare and valuable.

**2. Evidence is cited, not vibed.**  
P0/P2 items often point at concrete sites (README:47, benchstats.py:186, PR numbers, benchmark dirs, sim artifacts). That is the right grain for audit findings.

**3. Decision framing is mostly correct.**  
P1’s (a)/(b)/(c) options, #303 KEEP-t with residual as power, #302 kill-grid-keep-question, and “#252 stays blocked” are decision-shaped, not task-shaped — appropriate for a /decide doc.

**4. Scope honesty about ADOPT vs bespoke.**  
The 29-Jul ADOPT track note (Inspect AI substrate, what stays bespoke) prevents “rewrite the lab” drift. Keep that.

**5. Status header is useful as a dashboard.**  
P0 SHIPPED / P1 DECIDED / remaining work is a good living status block — for a *program* doc, not for an implementer.

---

## Critical gap: this is not executable as written

Against the writing-plans skill bar, an engineer cannot pick this up and ship.

| Writing-plans requires | This document has |
|---|---|
| Goal / Architecture / Tech stack header | Status paragraph + audit narrative |
| File structure map before tasks | Scattered file cites inside findings |
| Bite-sized tasks with TDD steps | Priority buckets (P0–P3) and /decide items |
| Exact code in every step | Recommendations and dispositions |
| Exact run commands + expected output | Occasional sim/result references |
| Interfaces between tasks | None |
| Checkbox task tracking | None |
| One independently testable deliverable per task | Multi-subsystem program of work |
| Save to `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md` | Looks like a plan in `~/.claude/plans/` style |

**Recommendation:** Keep this as the **source program doc / decision ledger**. Do **not** hand it to an implementer. Split into separate implementation plans after each /decide lands.

---

## Scope check (must split)

This covers at least **five independent subsystems**. One plan that tries to do all of them will thrash:

1. **Truth-in-labeling / docs hygiene** (P0 remainder + lows) — pure doc/copy, no measurement  
2. **P1 re-measure policy** (ADR amend + debt ledger + G≥8 batch protocol) — policy + process  
3. **Instrument dispositions** (#303, #317, #310, #302) — four separate /decide outcomes, different code surfaces  
4. **Naming** (skill-assay rename PR — already DECIDED, own PR, last) — packaging/rename  
5. **ADOPT track** (Inspect AI substrate ~10pd) — architecture swap  
6. **Lever-1 product work** (building-skills iter4, optimizing-context re-measure) — skill content + benchmarks  

Writing-plans rule: *if multiple independent subsystems, one plan per subsystem, each producing working testable software.*

Suggested plan set (after remaining decides):

| Plan | Depends on | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| A. Residual P0 lows (if any unshipped) | nothing | Honest labels only |
| B. P1 re-measure debt ledger + ADR text | owner /decide (DECIDED?) | Policy + ledger file, no spend |
| C. #303 close + docs/tests for KEEP-t / G≥8 | /decide | Issue closed + any code/docs that encode the rule |
| D. #317 overlap report + future-benchmark rule | /decide | Standing caveat artifact + ADR/rule |
| E. #310 round-2 sweep + residual-risk ADR | /decide | One consolidated sweep, then ADR |
| F. #302 lean edits + free read + C5 pre-reg (no $25 grid) | /decide | Content edits + pre-reg doc |
| G. skill-assay rename | owner merge consent | Rename PR only |
| H. Lever-1: building-skills iter4 | P1 bar settled | Char-negative skill reshape + measure |
| I. Lever-1: optimizing-context re-measure | P1 + G≥8 | Benchmark run + verdict |
| J. Inspect AI ADOPT | own /decide + ADR | Adapter-backed substrate (large; own design doc first) |

Anything still “owner /decide” should **not** be in an implementation plan yet — only in this ledger.

---

## Section-by-section feedback

### Status header
**Strength:** Excellent program memory.  
**Risk:** It is dense enough that a new reader will treat DECIDED as DONE. Separate:

- **Decided (waiting merge / waiting execution)**  
- **Implemented**  
- **Blocked on /decide**

Explicitly list open PRs and merge gates (you already mention verifier/red-team/grok/session-operator for #321 — good; mirror that pattern for every remaining item).

### P0 — truth-in-labeling
**Strength:** Cheapest, highest-confidence work; line-level cites.  
**Weakness as implementation guidance:**

- Items 1–9 are a checklist, not tasks. No “write failing check / fix / commit” loop.  
- Item 8 (“defer to the script… budgeted file: measure headroom first”) mixes a product change with a measurement prerequisite — split or defer entirely under YAGNI until lever-1 work needs it.  
- Item 9 “fix in passing” is fine for audit; for implementation, either promote to explicit steps with exact before/after strings or drop from the plan.  
- If PR #320 already shipped P0, **mark each of 1–9 as SHIPPED or REMAINING**. A plan that re-lists shipped work invites double-edits.

### P1 — “never on faith”
**Strength:** Correct that G≈6 MDE undermines per-edit re-measure; (b)+batched G≥8 is coherent.  
**Missing for an implementer:**

- Exact ADR text changes (which sections of 0024/README).  
- Shape of the “re-measure debt ledger” (file path, schema: skill, commit range, last measured dir, debt reason, unlock condition).  
- What “batched re-measure at G≥8” means operationally (case count, budget cap, judge family, pass/fail rule).  
- How #252 unblocks after P1 (one sentence is not an interface).

Until those exist, this stays a /decide outcome, not a plan.

### P2 — instrument decisions
**Strength:** Evidence-heavy; recommendations are mostly decisive.  
**Problems:**

- **#303:** “KEEP t” is a disposition. Implementation plan needs: which docs/tests encode interval family, what to change if anything, issue close checklist. If the answer is “close issue, no code,” say that explicitly so YAGNI holds.  
- **#317:** “per-benchmark overlap report as standing caveat” needs path, generator script or manual template, and where the caveat is *surfaced* (README? benchmark report? gate?). “Require task-value outcomes for FUTURE benchmarks” needs the exact rule text and enforcement mechanism (validate? human checklist? ADR only?).  
- **#310:** “one consolidated round 2… then residual-risk ADR regardless of quiet” is good sequencing. Still not a task list: what are the round-2 checks, against which files, what “quiet” means, ADR template.  
- **#302:** Best of the set — (i)(ii)(iii) are almost task-shaped. Still needs: the 4 exact reference-file edits (~800 chars), file paths, and the C5 pre-reg document skeleton. “Free read of obra’s remaining ~50k” is research, not an implementation task — park it outside the plan or time-box it as a spike with a written output path.

### P2b — naming
**Strength:** Collision research is real; complement-vs-substitute verdict is sound.  
**Status conflict:** Header says skill-assay rename CONFIRMED and executes LAST in own PR; body still says “Decide: rename vs README disambiguation.” Resolve to one line: **DECIDED rename; README disambiguation was interim; execution PR is last.**

### P3 — lever 1
**Strength:** Stop-list is the highest-leverage paragraph in the doc.  
**Weakness:** “building-skills iteration 4 (char-negative reshape)” is a project, not a plan. Needs the iter3 ledger pointer, target char budget, which sections to cut/move, and measure protocol after P1. Same for optimizing-context.

### /sweep evaluation
**Strength:** Honest that paired measurement is queued; resists fake KEEP.  
**Placement:** This is audit of `/sweep`, not part of the consistency program’s implementation. Keep as appendix or link out so it does not look like a delivery workstream.

### ADOPT track (in status header)
**Risk:** A ~10pd substrate swap buried in a status paragraph will either be ignored or swallowed into “alignment work.”  
**Ask:** Separate design doc + own plan. Adapter seam note is the right starting architecture sentence — expand there, not here.

---

## Taste / process risks (questionable-taste engineer lens)

The writing-plans skill assumes the implementer has **questionable taste**. This document still leaves room to fail:

1. **Ceremony expansion** — P3 says stop expanding pdca ceremony, but P2 still has residual-risk ADRs, overlap reports, debt ledgers, pre-regs. That can be correct *and* still recreate the spiral. For each artifact, require one sentence: *who reads this before a ship decision?* If nobody, cut.  
2. **Measurement as progress** — grok’s self-deception call is still the main hazard. Any implementation plan derived from this should put **lever-1 tasks on the critical path** and instrument closes as *enablers*, not as the milestone.  
3. **Underpowered science theater** — G≥8 is stated; encode it as a hard gate in the plan (commands that refuse G<8 for strong claims), not as prose.  
4. **No TDD story** — even doc-only work can have checks (`validate.py`, adr-lint, grep for retired ADR cites, tombstone path existence). Plans should fail a command first, then fix.  
5. **No commit cadence** — “one PR for P0” was fine; remaining work needs “commit after each green task.”  
6. **Placeholders by another name** — “route the 38 by rung,” “lean reference-file edits,” “char-negative reshape,” “free read” are soft TODOs. Writing-plans forbids them unless expanded to exact content.

---

## Self-review checklist applied to *this* doc

**1. Spec coverage:** There is no single product spec — it is multi-spec. Coverage is good as a program map; coverage as implementation is incomplete for every unshipped item except parts of #302.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Fails. Multiple “recommend / route / apply the 4 edits / reshape” without content.

**3. Type/consistency:** Naming is inconsistent across the doc (skill-bench vs skill-assay; DECIDED rename vs still-decide; P0 list vs SHIPPED). Fix the status vocabulary once and reuse.

---

## What I would tell the author to do next

1. **Freeze this document’s role:** “Program ledger + decision log.” Stop growing it into a mega-plan.  
2. **Close remaining /decides** (#310, #317, #302 if not already; #303 close-ready) with one-line dispositions in the header.  
3. **Write one implementation plan per unblocked workstream**, starting with whatever is actually unblocked today (likely residual P0 lows if any, then #303 close, then #302 lean edits if decided — *not* Inspect AI first).  
4. **Each plan** gets the required header, file map, Interfaces blocks, full TDD steps, exact commands, no TBD.  
5. **Put lever-1 on the calendar** as soon as P1’s bar is mergeable — otherwise the ledger will keep winning.

---

## Bottom line

| Dimension | Grade | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Diagnosis quality | A | Strong, evidenced, correctly suspicious of the lab |
| Decision framing | A− | Clear options; a few still open |
| Execution readiness | D | Not an implementation plan |
| Scope discipline | C | Too many subsystems in one doc |
| YAGNI / anti-spiral | B+ | Stop-list good; artifact load still high |
| Zero-context engineer | F | Cannot implement from this alone |

**Do not execute this document as a plan.** Promote dispositions to ADRs/issues, then author thin, subsystem-scoped plans under `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>.md`.

---

If you want a next step from me, pick one:

1. **Rewrite this into a program ledger** (status-only, no fake tasks) + a **recommended plan split** with filenames.  
2. **Author the first real implementation plan** for the highest-priority *unblocked* workstream (tell me which: residual P0, #303 close, #302 lean edits, skill-assay rename, or lever-1 prep).  
3. **Draft the P1 debt-ledger + ADR amend plan** as the gate that unblocks #252 and re-measures.

Which approach?
